examples.label: positive
negative

value.reason: The public POST /rest/user/reset-password route (server.ts:637) loads a user with UserModel.findByPk(data.UserId) without an attributes restriction. It then returns the whole updated Sequelize instance with res.json({ user: updatedUser }). The User model includes sensitive fields that the route doesn't need to return: the password hash (from security.hash), redacted secret/token fields, lastLoginIp, profileImage, email and username. The Evidence shows no attribute allow-list, no toJSON override and no field filtering. Anyone who completes the security-question reset therefore gets back the account's complete record, including credential material. This matches the positive example, where findByPk is followed by res.json of the full model, and it is a case of returning every object property (broken object property level authorization). Personal data is not protected by limiting what the response contains.
